questions.question: As per Global Hunger Index (GHI) 2022, India ranks at ______ position.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **107th**

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points:__**

__
 
• India has been ranked 107th out of 121 countries in the 2022 Global Hunger Index (GHI) released on 14th October 2022.
 
• In 2021, India was ranked 101st out of 116 countries.
 
• India has fared poorer than its neighbors Pakistan (99th), Nepal (81st) and Bangladesh (84th).
 
• The index calculates the hunger levels and malnutrition across the world.
 
• Published by: Concern Worldwide and Welthungerhilfe

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points:__**

 
• This year, the report accessed data from 136 countries but evaluated 121 of them. 
 
• The Global Hunger Index score is calculated on four indicators – undernourishment, child wasting (the share of children under the age of five with low weight for their height), child stunting (children under the age of five with low height for their age) and child mortality (the mortality rate of children under the age of five).
 
• India’s global hunger index score is 29.1, which puts the country in the “serious” category of hunger problems.
 
• In 2021, India's score was 27.5.
 
• Lesser GHI score means better ranking in the index.
 
• Globally, 17 countries, including China, Hungary, Montenegro, Uzbekistan, Russia and Saudi Arabia, shared the top spot.
 
• No country has been placed in the extremely alarming category this year.

questions.question: What is the full form of EPROM?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Erasable Programmable Read-Only Memory.__

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points:__**

__
 
• ​EPROM (Erasable Programmable Read-Only Memory) is a form of computer memory. 
 
• It does not lose its content when the power supply is cut off and that can be erased and reused.
 
• EPROMs are generally employed for programs designed for repeated use but that can be upgraded with a later version of a program.
 
• EPROMs are erased with ultraviolet light.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__**

 
• The EPROMs have been upgraded with extended capability as an EEPROM (Electrically Erasable Programmable Read-Only Memory).
 
• Flash memory, which is extensively used in computers is an EEPROM.

• An atom is any particle of matter at its most basic level which contains at least one proton. 
 
• Molecules are made up of one or more atoms.

• Monoatomic molecules
 
• Diatomic molecules
 
• Triatomic molecules
 
 

Explanation:__

Monoatomic molecules:

__
 
• A molecule composed of just one atom, and lacking any covalent bonds. 
 
• The noble gases such as He, Ne, Ar, Kr, Xe, and Rn are monoatomic molecules.

Triatomic molecules:

 
• Triatomic molecules are molecules composed of three atoms, of either the same or different chemical elements.
 
• An example is ozone.

questions.question: The First Amendment Act, 1951 of the Indian constitution added which of the following schedules?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ninth schedule**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ninth schedule**
 
• Ninth Schedule of the Indian Constitution pertains to protect the state laws pertaining to land reforms from being challenged in the Judiciary.
 
• However, Judicial review was made a part of the Basic Structure of the Constitution after the Keshavananda Bharti Case.
 
• Further, the Coehlo case made a judgement where subjects from the ninth schedule couldn't be kept immune from judicial review.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Schedules
 Features of Schedules
 
 

 1st Schedule
 It contains the name of States and Union Territories.
 
 

 2nd Schedule
 The provisions in relation to allowances, privileges, and emoluments
 
 

 3rd Schedule
 Oath and affirmation
 
 

 
 
 

 4th Schedule
 It contains the provisions in relation to the allocation of seats for States and Union Territories in the Rajya Sabha
 
 

 5th Schedule
 It contains provisions in relation to the administration and control of scheduled areas and scheduled tribes
 
 

 6th Schedule
 It contains provisions in relation to the administration of tribal areas in the states of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram
 
 

 7th Schedule
 This schedule deals with the three legislative lists
 
 

 8th Schedule
 It deals with the 22 official languages recognized by the Constitution:
 
 

 9th Schedule
 It deals with the state acts and regulations of that deal with land reforms and the abolition of the Zamindari system. It also deals with the acts and regulations of the Parliament dealing with other matters.
 
 

 10th Schedule
 It contains provisions relating to disqualification of the members of Parliament and State Legislatures on the ground of defection.
 
 

 11th Schedule
 It contains the provisions that specify the powers, authority and responsibilities of Panchayats.
 
 

 12th Schedule
 It deals with the provisions that specify the powers, authority and responsibilities of Municipalities.

• Asteroids have their orbits between Mars and Jupiter. In the past, planets and their moons have existed between Mars and Jupiter in the asteroid belt.
 
• They were destroyed in some kind of affliction. The asteroids belt could be their scattered remains. Hence, the combined gravitational force of Jupiter and Mars accelerates the moving of the asteroids around them.
 
• Ceres, Vesta, Pallas and Hygiea are few names of Asteroids.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: What is the name of the mascot for 36th National Games, 2022?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Savaj**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

The 36th National Games

 
• The 36th National Games is coming to an end after a glorious display of sporting performance and sportsmanship spirit.
 
• In its 36th edition, Gujarat hosted the National Games for the first time in 2022.
 
• The National Games 2022 was held across six cities, Ahmedabad, Gandhinagar, Surat, Vadodara, Rajkot, and Bhavnagar, in Gujarat.
 
• Almost 7,000 athletes from 28 Indian States, eight Union Territories, and Services, the sports team of the Indian Armed Forces, competed for medals in 36 different sports.
 
• The Official mascot for the 36th National Games is “SAVAJ”, it portrays a sportsman’s most prominent personality traits of self-confidence, vigor, a strong sense of motivation, an inner desire to succeed, a strong sense of focus, a natural leader, and a goal setter
 
 
• Savaj- taranhar in gujarati means “Savior” in English. Savaj is the representation of The Asiatic Lion, which today survives only in wild India.
 
 
 
• National Games
 
 
• ​The National Games trace its origins to the Olympic Movement, which became highly popular in India in the 1920s.
 
• The National Games of India was organized as the Indian Olympic Games in the initial years.
 
• Since the 9th edition of the 1924 Indian Olympic Games in Lahore, these games have been held every two years in major cities of India.
 
• In 1940, the Indian Olympic Games were organized as National Games.
 
• It involves competition between sportsmen from various parts of the country.
 
• The city of Lucknow in Uttar Pradesh hosted the inaugural edition of the National Games in Independent India.
 
• These games’ duration and regulations are within the jurisdiction of the Indian Olympics Association.
 
• The National Games must be conducted in such a way that they do not clash with the Olympic Games and Asian Games.

questions.question: If there are N firms in the economy, each assigned with a serial number from 1 to N, then as per the product method, GDP can be written as ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**GVA1 + GVA2 ..... + GVAN**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** Gross Domestic Product:

 
• Definition:

 
 
• GDP is the final value of the goods and services produced within the geographic boundaries of a country during a specified period of time, normally a year.
 
• GDP is the total value of all final goods and services produced during a particular year.
 
• GDP growth rate is an important indicator of the economic performance of a country.
 
• It counts the goods and services produced within the country and hence does not consider the products that the country imports from another country.
 
• It can be measured by three methods, namely,
 
• Output Method:
 
 
• This measures the monetary or market value of all the goods and services produced within the borders of the country.
 
• In order to avoid a distorted measure of GDP due to price level changes, GDP at constant prices o real GDP is computed. GDP (as per output method) = Real GDP (GDP at constant prices) – Taxes + Subsidies.
 
 
 
• Expenditure Method:
 
 
• This measures the total expenditure incurred by all entities on goods and services within the domestic boundaries of a country.
 
• GDP (as per expenditure method) = C + I + G + (X-IM) C: Consumption expenditure, I: Investment expenditure, G: Government spending and (X-IM): Exports minus imports, that is, net exports.
 
 
 
• Income Method:
 
 
• It measures the total income earned by the factors of production, that is, labour and capital within the domestic boundaries of a country.
 
• GDP (as per income method) = GDP at factor cost + Taxes – Subsidies.

questions.question: What is the average height of inner Himalayas?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**6000 metres**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The average height of the Inner Himalayas is 6000 meters__.
 
• Greater Himalayas
 __
 
• It is also called as Inner Himalayas or Himadri.
 
• It is the most continuous range consisting of the loftiest peaks.
 
• The average height of these peaks is 6,000 metres.
 
• It contains all prominent Himalayan peaks.
 
• The core of this part of the Himalayas is composed of granite.
 
• It is perennially snowbound, and a number of glaciers descend from this range.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Himachal or Lesser Himalayas

 
 
• This range lies to the south of the Himadri and forms the most rugged mountain system.
 
• The ranges are mainly composed of highly compressed and altered rocks.
 
• The altitude varies between 3,700 and 4,500 metres and the average width is of 50 Km.
 
• Pir Panjal, the Dhaula Dhar and the Mahabharat ranges are important ranges in the Himalayas.
 
• This range consists of the famous valley of Kashmir, the Kangra and the Kullu Valley in Himachal Pradesh.
 
• This region is well-known for its hill stations.
 
 
 
• Shivalik Range
 
 
• It is the outermost range of the Himalayas.
 
• They extend over a width of 10-50 Km and have an altitude varying between 900 and 1100 metres.
 
• The longitudinal valley lying between lesser Himalayas and the Shiwaliks is known as Duns.
 
• Dehra Dun, Kotli Dun and Patli Dun are some of the well-known Duns

The correct answer is __**Facilities for instruction in mother-tongue at primary stage**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Part XVII of the Indian Constitution deals with the official languages in Articles 343 to 351.
 
• Article 350A: (Facilities for instruction in mother-tongue at the primary stage) provides that it shall be the endeavour of every State and of every local authority within the State to provide adequate facilities for instruction in the mother-tongue at the primary stage of education to children belonging to linguistic minority groups.
 
• Article 350B: (Special Officer for linguistic minorities): The President should appoint a special officer for linguistic minorities to investigate all matters relating to the constitutional safeguards for linguistic minorities and to report to him. The President should place all such reports before the Parliament and send them to the state government concerned.
 
• Article 351: (Directive for development of the Hindi language) provides that it shall be the duty of the Union to promote the spread of the Hindi language.

questions.question: Which Indian festival celebrates the birth anniversary of spiritual leader Padmasambhava, founder of Tibet Tantric Buddhism?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hemis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Two-day long annual Hemis festival dedicated to the Guru Padmasambhava began on 26 June 2015 in the largest monastery of Ladakh Hemis Gompa (monastery).
 
• Hemis festival is celebrated to mark the birth anniversary of Guru Padmasambhava.
 
 
• During this festive season, Lamas called 'chhams,' perform masked dances and sacred plays to the accompaniment of cymbals, drums, and longhorns. The head lama presides over the function.
 
 
 
• The festival takes an auspicious turn every 12 years in the Tibetan Year of the Monkey when the two-storey-high Thanka depicting Padmasambhava is displayed.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Bakrid

 
 
• Bakrid is known as Id-ul-Zuha.
 
• Id-ul-Zuha (Bakr-Id), is a festival of great rejoice, special prayers, and exchange of greetings and gifts mark this festival of Muslims.
 
• Id-ul-Zuha, the festival of sacrifice is celebrated with traditional fervor and gaiety in India and the world.
 
• It is called Id-ul-Adha in Arabic and Bakr-Id in the Indian subcontinent, because of the tradition of sacrificing a goat or 'bakr' in Urdu. 
 
 

 
• Losar

 
 
• The Losar Festivals are celebrated in Arunachal Pradesh.
 
• It is celebrated by the people of the Monpa Tribe who are said to be inhabitants of Arunachal Pradesh.
 
• Losar is a 3-day festival, which is celebrated with great pomp and show in Tawang.
 
• The festival is observed to ward off evil spirits and welcome the new year that shall be filled with happiness and prosperity.
 
 
 
• ​GurPurab
 
 
• In the Sikh tradition, a GurPurab is a celebration of the anniversary of the birth of a guru, marked by a festival.
 
• The word Gur Purab first appeared in the days of the gurus. 
 
• It is a compound of the word Purab (or Parva in Sanskrit), with the word guru, indicating a festival or celebration. 
 
• According to the controversial Bhai Bala Janamsakhi, Guru Nanak was born on the Full Moon (Pooranmashi) of the Kartik Indian Lunar Month.
